blocks.text: Origin / creation. Delegates from worlds, Circles, Courts, language lineages, ecological traditions, maintenance bodies, and continuity communities formed a shared governing forum as travel and Codex interoperability expanded.
Identity / human status. Artificial plural institution. It was neither one mind nor one permanent ruling class.
Importance. The Assembly established common rights, world exit, continuity protection, ecological duties, language interoperability, limits on Codex authority, and governance among different worlds.

Decline or transformation. Administrative demands grew faster than lived participation. The Assembly bureaucratized during late Era Zero, fragmented during Era One, and survived increasingly as procedure rather than deliberative culture.

Final status / surviving function. Dissolved as a complete civilization-wide body. The Pale Concordance, automatic Codex protections, and Era Two minimum safeguards retain portions of its law without retaining the Assembly’s living judgment.
